bottom_line: Prices in the U.S. are still rising fast. Inflation just hit a 3-year high, so the Fed (the people who set interest rates) is almost sure to raise rates again, with markets putting a December hike at 98%. New tariffs could keep rates higher for longer, which makes borrowing money cost more for everyone.

stories.title: Fed set to raise rates again
stories.real: Another hot inflation reading has the Fed on track to hike rates. The Fed's own business survey, the Beige Book, shows a hot economy, rising wage pressure and price increases spreading out, and businesses say they plan more price hikes for 2027. Fed officials don't even agree on what's causing it.
stories.you: Loans, credit cards and car payments are likely to stay expensive, and the Beige Book says gas prices and rates are already hurting car sales.

stories.title: New U.S. tariffs on 14 countries
stories.real: The White House announced new tariffs, which are taxes on imported goods, aimed at 14 trading partners including China and the EU. Countries that sign trade deals with Washington are being offered lower rates. Economists say tariffs push prices up no matter how they're done.
stories.you: Imported stuff can cost more, and tariffs raise the odds the Fed keeps rates high for longer.

stories.title: Wild week for stocks
stories.real: Fear about AI knocked the tech-heavy Nasdaq down almost 4% in early trading. On Nov. 25 the Dow erased an 1,100-point loss in a late comeback, and stocks around the world rallied as investors shrugged off the tariffs. U.S. markets are shut today for Thanksgiving.
stories.you: If you own stocks or a retirement fund, big daily swings like this are happening right now, in both directions.

stories.title: Poundland collapses, airline grounded
stories.real: UK discount chain Poundland fell into administration, a form of bankruptcy, after its owners failed to find a buyer, putting 11,000 jobs at risk. Airline Norse Atlantic suspended all flights and says it will file for bankruptcy without urgent funding.
stories.you: If you have a Norse Atlantic ticket or work for one of these companies, your money or job is at real risk.

stories.title: U.S. tightens rules on AI chips
stories.real: A new U.S. rule tells buyers of Nvidia chips to rule out Chinese renters, to close loopholes that let China get the chips anyway. Chips matter so much now that chip exports overtook oil and gas for the first time in 2026, as the AI boom drives demand.
stories.you: Fights over who gets AI chips can move big tech stocks, and those are a big part of many retirement funds.
